messages:
emily: Quick head's up 1 - spotted inconsistent rate-limit header casing and retry semantics in the docs for streaming endpoints. In streaming.md the curl example shows `x-ratelimit-limit: 100` but the SSE section references `X-RateLimit-Limit`. Also the doc text says clients should wait the value in `Retry-After` (seconds) for HTTP 429 *and* for SSE throttles, but runtime emits `Retry-After-ms` for SSE where the unit is milliseconds.

omar: ouch. which files are affected?

emily: streaming.md and api-ref/common-headers.md. The SDK snippet for Node also reads `resp.headers['retry-after']` and treats it as seconds which will be broken for SSE flows that currently send ms.

jin: runtime team here 1 - we emit `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (canonical pascal-case) over HTTP. For SSE we currently send lowercase `x-ratelimit-limit` because of an internal proxy; that was an oversight. For throttling events over the SSE channel we include `retry-after-ms` (lowercase) representing milliseconds to wait. We can change the proxy to normalize SSE header names to the canonical form, but changing units for SSE will be breaking. Better option: update docs and SDKs to accept both `Retry-After` (seconds) and `Retry-After-Ms`/`retry-after-ms` (milliseconds) and add a migration note.

omar: I prefer standardizing casing in docs (use X-RateLimit-Limit) and explicitly call out the SSE-only `retry-after-ms` header unit. We should also update SDK examples to parse both header names and convert ms->s when needed.

emily: proposed doc text patch: "Rate-limit headers are emitted with canonical casing `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`. For streaming/ SSE events, some proxies emit lowercase header names and runtime may include `Retry-After-Ms` (or `retry-after-ms`) describing a backoff in milliseconds. Clients should prefer `Retry-After` (seconds) for HTTP 429, and fall back to reading `Retry-After-Ms` (milliseconds) for SSE events. Example conversion: `wait_seconds = int(retry_after_ms) / 1000.0`."

jin: ACK. We'll also push a tiny proxy patch to normalize header casing for SSE to reduce surprises (INF-1204). But docs change + SDK fallback is safest short term.

omar: can someone update the Node and Python SDK snippets? Node currently has: ```js
const wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'] || 0, 10);
setTimeout(() => retry(), wait * 1000);
```
Change to: ```js
let wait = 0;
if (resp.headers['retry-after']) wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'], 10);
else if (resp.headers['retry-after-ms']) wait = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after-ms'], 10) / 1000;
setTimeout(() => retry(), wait * 1000);
```

emily: I'll open a docs PR to update the two markdown pages and add codeblock language hints. Jin / infra will file INF-1204 to normalize SSE proxy headers. Omar, can you open the SDK snippets PR to add fallback parsing?

omar: PR created for sdk-snippets: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-snippets/pull/523 - adds Node + Python fallback parsing and a unit test asserting both header names are handled. sdk-ci: test fails in CI because the docs generator expects exact header names in examples.

docs-bot: docs PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/821 - CI: failed (example-schema-check) because I forgot to add the codeblock language hint on one snippet.

emily: fixing docs PR now (adding ```js and ```python for code blocks) and adding a short migration note: "Older streaming examples used Retry-After (seconds) uniformly; streaming may emit Retry-After-Ms (milliseconds) - SDKs now parse both."

docs-bot: docs PR CI: re-run -> passing. sdk-ci: sdk-snippets PR CI re-run: passing.

jin: infra ticket INF-1204 created to normalize SSE header casing; target next deploy.

emily: merging docs PR and adding a changelog entry: "streaming: clarified rate-limit header casing and added guidance for Retry-After-Ms (SSE milliseconds) with SDK fallback examples."

omar: will cut a patch release of SDK snippets tomorrow and include the note in the SDK changelog.

emily: thanks team. small follow-up: can we add a one-line in streaming.md that advises users to prefer the canonical headers `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and to handle both forms for now?

jin: done in the PR. Closing loop. :white_check_mark:
